narrative:
The model estimates you have a 19% chance of not passing your final year, which is above the 10% threshold that requires additional support. This doesn’t mean failure is certain, but it does mean the system has identified some risk factors that could make success harder for you.

The most important factor working in your favor is that you’ve never failed a class before. This strong track record suggests you have the ability to do well when you apply yourself. Another positive sign is that you chose this school because of its reputation, which often means you care about your education and want a good learning environment.

However, the model also noticed that you’ve said you want to go on to higher education. While this ambition is great, the system sees it as a potential risk because students who set very high goals sometimes struggle if they don’t have the right support in place. This factor slightly increased the predicted risk of not passing.

The main concern is that your family relationships are currently rated as very bad. This is quite rare—most students report good or very good family relationships—and it seems to be the biggest red flag. Difficult home situations can make it harder to focus on schoolwork, manage stress, or get the encouragement you need.

Because of these findings, you’re required to take remedial courses. This isn’t a punishment—it’s a chance to strengthen your skills and get extra support. Focus on using this time to build good study habits, and consider talking to a counselor about ways to improve your home environment. You have the potential to succeed, and these courses are here to help you do just that.
